bodies.clearance_source: default: Prusa's "at least 0.3 mm" for movable parts (fdm_fit)

checked: the exported mesh is closed, manifold and consistently wound, and the STEP agrees with it (valid, checks)
bounds, size, volumes and solid count of the exported files
whether each solid stands on the print plate (Z = 0 of the exported frame) or rests on a solid that does, and whether any reaches below it (bodies; failures are in problems)

what PURPOSE says it is for, compiled into requirements and evaluated on use(): the held objects, the mounts, the loads at each mount and whether it faces its user (purpose; anything not passing is in purpose.blocked)
not_checked: fit to the real object or a mating part (use cad_check_fit per state)
strength, stiffness or how it holds under load
motion, articulated poses and snap or flex behaviour
printing: supports, bridges and bed adhesion are the slicer's answer

purpose.for: holds my phone on the Forester's dash so I can see the map
purpose.modelled_on: a dash phone mount with an adhesive pad

requirements.says: held:phone sits on the part (0.00 mm)

requirements.fix: Model the dash as world:dash in use(): a solid slab where it really is, touching the part where it is taped, so the tape mount can be checked

requirements.says: phone's exposed face is 41 deg off the line to the user's eye (allowed 25)
requirements.fix: Turn the phone toward the user: its face is 41 deg off the line to their eye (allowed 25). Aim it the way the bought products do, with a joint or an angled base, and show it aimed in use()

requirements.says: phone is 812 mm from the user (allowed 700)
requirements.fix: Bring the phone within reach: it is 812 mm from the user (allowed 700)
